_doc: Drafted by the Profiler on issue #21 and re-verified against commit 79ffcf0 in a later run of issue #54. Every command in `commands` was executed on a clean checkout in the repo's own Actions runner; every other field is cited to a file read or a command run in the PR body.
estate_role: Standalone. Compass — a read-mostly lens and control panel over the Claude Software Factory (GitHub + OpenSpec). The product was named "Factory Console" until 709f5da (#82) renamed every user-facing string; the repo, the package scopes and the env names were deliberately left alone, so the code still says `console` everywhere (see gotchas). It has no sibling repos in this estate: it consumes GitHub's API and mirrors claude-software-factory's label/state contract in packages/core/src/factory.ts, but nothing in this estate depends on it, so there is no cross-repo merge order to honour. It also forwards GitHub events to the factory's LangGraph orchestrator over HTTP (packages/core/src/orchestrator-client.ts, ORCHESTRATOR_URL) — a runtime dependency on a service, not a repo dependency. MIT-licensed and being prepared for public release (.github/REPOSITORY_SETTINGS.md), so treat anything committed here as publishable.
stack: TypeScript end-to-end (ES2022, module NodeNext, strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), Node >=20.19, pnpm 10.33 workspace. apps/api = Fastify 5 (@fastify/cookie, GitHub OAuth, REST, webhook endpoint); apps/worker = BullMQ 5 on ioredis (webhook projection, reconciler, OpenSpec scaffolding, orchestrator event forwarding); apps/web = React 18 + Vite 6 SPA (react-router-dom 6, @tanstack/react-query 5; tested with Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library, and a Playwright + @axe-core/playwright responsive suite); packages/core = factory constants, hidden-comment markers, state derivation, the routing-policy modules the Console renders factory decisions from, two-token GitHub REST client (jose + libsodium-wrappers), AES-256-GCM envelope crypto, zod env config; packages/db = Drizzle ORM 0.45 over Postgres 16 (postgres.js driver) with hand-rolled forward-only SQL migrations; packages/insight = Anthropic SDK plus OpenAI-compatible providers (openai, grok, openrouter) for cited, read-only Q&A. Deployed as Docker images (infra/Dockerfile.api, infra/Dockerfile.web) behind nginx and Traefik on a VPS.
conventions: pnpm workspace, ESM only. Every package is `"type": "module"` and tsconfig is `module: NodeNext`, so relative imports MUST carry the `.js` extension even in TypeScript sources (`import { loadEpic } from "./read.js"`). Cross-package imports use the workspace aliases `@console/core`, `@console/db`, `@console/insight`.

API routes are `registerXRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, deps: AppDeps): void` in apps/api/src/routes/*.ts, wired once in apps/api/src/app.ts. Dependencies (config, db handle, credential store, BullMQ queues) are threaded through the `AppDeps` object — no module-level singletons, which is what lets the tests build the whole app against an in-process Postgres.

Every authenticated route starts with `const ctx = await requireAuth(deps, req, reply); if (!ctx) return;` and then scopes each query to `ctx.orgIds` at the data layer (`inArray(table.orgId, ctx.orgIds)`). Authorisation is a WHERE clause, not a post-filter. Errors are returned as `reply.code(N).send({ error: "lowercase message" })`.

There is a second, narrower auth path for instance-wide routes, and only two kinds of route may use it: `setupAccess(deps, req)` in apps/api/src/setup.ts, which admits the GitHub App owner (or, before the App is configured, the bootstrap operator / `APP_RESET`) and returns `{ allowed, ctx }` for the caller to refuse with 403. It exists because some data spans every estate on the instance rather than one caller's orgs — the ingestion log in apps/api/src/routes/ops.ts and the setup/onboarding flow — so `ctx.orgIds` is the wrong question there. Those routes are therefore NOT org-scoped by design. Everything else uses `requireAuth`: reach for `setupAccess` only when the route is genuinely instance-wide and owner-only, and say so in design.md.

Two-token model as a structural property (packages/core/src/github.ts): `InstallationClient` is the App's identity (reads, non-authoritative comments); `UserClient` is the human's OAuth identity. Anything carrying authority — approving, merging, labelling, filing issues — exists only on `UserClient` and is reached via `userClient(deps, ctx)`. Do not add an authoritative operation to `InstallationClient`.

Database access is Drizzle query-builder only (`db.select().from(x).where(and(eq(...)))`) — no raw SQL strings in app code. Schema lives in packages/db/src/schema.ts and is split by comment banner into GitHub PROJECTIONS (keyed by `gh_node_id`, guarded by `gh_updated_at`, rebuildable, never backed up) and CONSOLE-NATIVE tables. No table mixes the two.

Secrets are never stored in the clear: OAuth tokens, the GitHub App private key and cached repo content go through `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` (AES-256-GCM under `CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY`, `v1.iv.tag.ct` envelope). Environment variables are declared and validated in the zod schema in packages/core/src/config.ts and read as `cfg.X` — never `process.env` in app code.

Request bodies are validated by hand against Fastify's generic type parameters (`app.post<{ Body: {...} }>(...)` then explicit checks returning 400). zod is imported in exactly one source file — packages/core/src/config.ts, for environment config — so a second zod import is a deliberate change of style: say so in design.md rather than slipping it in.

Factory routing rules live in packages/core as pure functions over labels and state, never inline in a route or a component: epic-status.ts, next-step.ts, start-gate.ts, plan-tests.ts, test-verdict.ts, bug-report.ts, testing-policy.ts. Each opens with a block comment citing the FACTORY.md section it mirrors, and most have a same-named suite in packages/core/test. A new rule about what the factory does goes there, with its citation and its test; the route or component only renders the answer.

Comments explain *why*, not what: most modules open with a block comment citing the decision they implement — a plan/spec section (`spec 01 §2.2`, `plan 02 §1a`) or, for the factory-policy modules, the FACTORY.md section. New modules follow that — a reader should be able to get from the code to the decision that shaped it.

Anything the Console writes back to GitHub is an ordinary comment carrying a hidden marker (`<!-- console:thread=… -->`, `<!-- console:decision=… -->`, packages/core/src/markers.ts), built by `threadMarker()`/`decisionMarker()` rather than hand-written. That is what keeps the projection rebuildable and non-Console users first-class; never invent a new storage location for state that belongs on GitHub.

There is exactly one exception to 'the Console writes comments, not files', and it is for FACTORY CONFIG the factory itself reads: `.github/factory-approvers.json` is committed to each repo's default branch when an admin saves 'Who can release' (apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts, POST /api/projects/:id/permissions, added in fea2a69 / #83). It is a read-modify-write — `getFileAtRef` then `UserClient.putFile` with the previous blob's `sha`, spreading the parsed file so the other keys survive — committed as the signed-in user, never as the App, and the database mirror in `gateAssignments` is rewritten in the same request because the push webhook may not land before the next merge is attempted. Follow that whole shape if another factory config file ever needs the same treatment; do not write a file for anything the factory does not read from the repo.

Routes that change configuration are gated a third way, beyond `requireAuth` and `setupAccess`: `const found = await loadOrg(deps, ctx, orgId, reply, { admin: true }); if (!found) return;` (apps/api/src/routes/settings.ts). It resolves the org within `ctx.orgIds` and requires the caller's membership role to be `owner` or `admin`. An unknown org and a non-member both answer 404 (`org not found`), so a stranger cannot tell an org exists; only a member who is merely a member gets 403. Every write in routes/settings.ts and routes/projects.ts goes through it. A new configuration write that only calls `requireAuth` is under-gated: any org member could then change who may release.

Tenant scoping has exactly one escape hatch: `systemScope()` in packages/db/src/index.ts, used by the reconciler and webhook workers because they act across tenants by design. It is deliberately greppable — cross-tenant access that does not go through it is a bug, and adding a second escape hatch defeats the audit.

The SPA talks to the API only through the `api.get/post/del` wrapper in apps/web/src/api.ts (same-origin credentials plus the `x-console-csrf` header on writes). Pages live in src/pages, shared widgets in src/components, server state goes through TanStack Query; do not call `fetch()` directly from a component.
review_checklist: New or changed API route: does it call `requireAuth` and scope every query to `ctx.orgIds`? An unscoped `db.select()` in a route is a cross-tenant leak, and apps/api/test/memberships.test.ts exists because that boundary has been got wrong before. The one legitimate exception is an instance-wide, owner-only route gated by `setupAccess` and refusing with 403 — apps/api/src/routes/ops.ts is the existing example, and it is deliberately not org-scoped. Treat a NEW `setupAccess` route as a change request unless design.md argues for it; treat a route with neither guard as a leak.

State-changing route: it must be a non-GET method, so `requireAuth`'s CSRF-header check applies. A mutation behind `app.get` bypasses one of the two CSRF layers (there is deliberately no CORS — see the comment in apps/api/src/app.ts).

Authoritative GitHub operation (approve, merge, label, comment-as-user, file issue): must go through `userClient(deps, ctx)`, never `InstallationClient`. Check it also writes an `auditLog` row, as apps/api/src/routes/gate.ts and write.ts do.

A Console control that IS a factory gate must also check that this user holds that gate — `userClient` only proves who is asking, not that they may. `POST /api/prs/:id/merge` shipped without that check and any org member could merge a promotion PR from the Console; fea2a69 (#83) fixed it with `repoApprovers(deps, repoId, gate)` from apps/api/src/start-gate.ts, refusing with 403 and naming the people who may. Note the three rules it encodes, which a new control must match: the list is per REPO, not per estate (`loadApproversForGate` unions the estate, which is right for the queue and wrong for a merge); a base of the default branch is the `release` gate (G3) and of the integration branch the `staging` gate (GS), while spec and design PRs have their own gates and epic branches none; and an EMPTY list means 'any collaborator', so it must not be read as 'nobody' and an empty production list is refused at the point it is saved.

A dependabot PR can be a breaking upgrade in two different ways, and the `ignore` rule covers neither of them. (a) `.github/dependabot.yml` ignores `version-update:semver-major` for the **npm** and **docker** ecosystems only — the **github-actions** ecosystem has no `ignore` block at all, so Action majors merge straight through in a group called simply 'actions'. bde68c2 (#57) is the worked example: five semver-majors in one PR (actions/checkout 4→7, github/codeql-action 3→4, pnpm/action-setup 4→6, actions/setup-node 4→7, appleboy/scp-action 0.1.7→1.0.0). (b) On the npm side semver calls a 0.x minor a minor, and five dependencies here are 0.x: drizzle-orm, drizzle-kit, @electric-sql/pglite, @anthropic-ai/sdk, libsodium-wrappers — e059284 (#78) carried drizzle-orm 0.36.4 to 0.45.4, nine minors, inside a group titled 'minor-and-patch'. Read the Actions rows and the 0.x rows of the bump table on their own, and ask for the suite's output rather than the ignore rule's reassurance.

Schema change: is there a new numbered file in packages/db/migrations/ (NNNN_name.sql, statements separated by `--> statement-breakpoint`)? The runner is forward-only and lexicographic — editing an already-applied migration is silently a no-op on any deployed database.

Projection change: does the write still guard on `gh_updated_at` (last-writer-wins) and key on `gh_node_id`? Webhook delivery is at-least-once and out of order; a projection write without the guard reintroduces flapping state.

Secrets: any new credential must be stored via `encryptSecret` and any new environment variable declared in the zod schema in packages/core/src/config.ts. A raw token column or a bare `process.env` read is a change request.

Factory label/state constants and routing rules — packages/core/src/factory.ts plus the policy modules beside it (epic-status, next-step, start-gate, plan-tests, test-verdict, bug-report, testing-policy) — mirror claude-software-factory's FACTORY.md. Changing them to make the UI nicer desynchronises the Console from the factory: the Console renders factory state, it never invents it. A change here should cite the FACTORY.md section that moved.

A new or reworked SPA surface must hold at 360, 768 and 1280px with no horizontal pan and no new axe violation (apps/web/e2e/ux.spec.ts). No CI job runs that suite, so ask the author for the output of `pnpm --filter @console/web test:e2e` rather than assuming a green PR covered it.
Markdown from GitHub must stay sanitised server-side (apps/api/src/render.ts uses marked + sanitize-html). Rendering untrusted markdown anywhere else, or relaxing the sanitiser, is a change request.

Any new comment body the Console can post to GitHub: confirm it cannot trim to exactly one of the factory's five live trigger literals — `Approved` (G1/G2/GS and the task start), `Review Done`, `Test Passed`, `Test Failed`, `Plan tests`. They are `APPROVED_BODY`, `REVIEW_DONE_BODY`, `TEST_PASSED_BODY`, `TEST_FAILED_BODY` and `PLAN_TESTS_BODY` in packages/core/src/factory.ts, matched strictly (`isApprovedComment` in markers.ts), so an incidental exact match approves a gate or records a test verdict for real. Compose bodies from those constants rather than retyping the strings.
qa_notes: Vitest 2 throughout; `pnpm test` runs `pnpm -r test` across the workspace. Tests live in a `test/` directory beside `src/` (apps/api/test, apps/worker/test, packages/core/test, packages/insight/test), named `*.test.ts`.

`pnpm test` needs a prior `pnpm build` — run `commands.test` (`pnpm build && pnpm test`), not `pnpm test` on its own. packages/core, packages/db and packages/insight resolve to `./dist/index.js` through their package.json `main`/`exports`, `dist/` is gitignored, so on a clean checkout the consuming suites die at collection with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@console/core"` / `"@console/db"` and no test runs at all. Verified on this commit: a fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` followed straight by `pnpm test` exits 1 in 13s (apps/worker, 6 files failed, 'no tests'); after `pnpm build` the same command is green. The deploy workflow never trips over this because its `check` job builds first.

Measured on this commit: apps/api 28 files / 283 tests, packages/core 15 / 177, apps/web 20 / 121, apps/worker 6 / 53, packages/insight 1 / 8, packages/db 0 — 70 files and 642 tests in all, every one green. Only packages/db and packages/insight still carry `--passWithNoTests` (verified in their package.json `test` scripts); apps/web has a real jsdom suite, which grew by 2 files / 18 tests across #84 and #85, so that flag is no longer a reason to skip testing a UI change.

apps/web tests run under jsdom, configured in the `test` block of apps/web/vite.config.ts (not a separate vitest.config.ts): `setupFiles: ./src/test-setup.ts`, which pulls in @testing-library/jest-dom and registers `afterEach(cleanup)`. Component and page suites sit beside their subject as `*.test.tsx` under src/, and use Testing Library queries plus @testing-library/user-event. A new UI test needs no config change.

There is a Playwright + axe responsive suite at apps/web/e2e/ux.spec.ts, run by `pnpm --filter @console/web test:e2e`: it serves e2e.html on 127.0.0.1:4177 and asserts no horizontal pan and no axe violation at 360, 768 and 1280px. It is NOT part of `pnpm test` and NOT run by any CI job, and it needs `pnpm exec playwright install` first. This profile run read it rather than executing it — no Playwright browsers were present in the runner — so treat its pass/fail as unknown until someone runs it.

Integration tests boot a real in-process Postgres (`new PGlite()` from @electric-sql/pglite, drizzle-orm/pglite adapter) and apply every file in packages/db/migrations in `beforeAll`, then build the whole Fastify app via `buildApp(deps)`. See apps/api/test/security.test.ts for the canonical setup and apps/worker/test/helpers.ts for the worker equivalent. No Docker, no external database — a new suite should follow the same shape rather than mocking the database.

GitHub is never called for real: tests point `apiUrl` at `https://api.invalid` and inject fakes through `AppDeps` (e.g. `CredentialStore({ load: async () => null })` to exercise the environment fallback). Queues are replaced with in-memory arrays that record what was enqueued.

That PGlite warmup is why apps/api/vitest.config.ts and apps/worker/vitest.config.ts raise `testTimeout` to 30s (and the API's `hookTimeout` to 60s). A new suite that boots its own PGlite instance needs the same allowance.

A pull request now does get the full suite — this changed in 79ffcf0 (#86) and reverses what earlier profiles said. deploy.yml gained a `pull_request` trigger, so its `check` job (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm test`, named `typecheck-test-build`) runs on every PR, while the `deploy` job is held back by `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`; the same check runs again on the push to `main` as the final gate before the deploy. Two holes remain, both from the shared `paths-ignore` (`.github/**`, `**/*.md`, `docs/**`): a PR touching only those paths triggers NO check at all, so a markdown-only or workflow-only PR has nothing to go green and you must not wait for one; and CodeQL (`javascript-typescript` + `actions`, on push and PR) reports code-scanning alerts rather than failing a job. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is still gone (deleted in b91b168) — the suite lives in deploy.yml and nowhere else. A PR check can also be cancelled by a newer push to the same branch (`cancel-in-progress` is true for pull requests only), so read the latest run, not the first.

Typecheck is a real gate in that post-merge job — a change that compiles under `tsc --noEmit` in one package but not another fails it, and because it fails after merge it fails the deploy. Run `pnpm typecheck` across the workspace before handing work on, not just the package you touched.

apps/worker/test carries the projection invariants, including an explicit replay test — 'is idempotent and order-tolerant: shuffled + duplicated replay converges to the same state'. Any change to apps/worker/src/project.ts must keep that green and, if it adds a projected entity, extend it rather than adding a separate happy-path test.
gotchas: There is no linter or formatter in this repo — no eslint, prettier or biome config, and no package declares a `lint` script. The root `package.json` does have `"lint": "pnpm -r lint"`, but running it FAILS with `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` (verified, exit 1). `commands.lint` is null for that reason: treat a red `pnpm lint` as the absence of a gate, not as a defect introduced by your change.

Run `pnpm build` before `pnpm test` or nothing runs. The workspace packages are consumed through their built `dist/`, which is gitignored, so `pnpm test` on a clean checkout fails at import resolution (`Failed to resolve entry for package "@console/core"`) rather than on any assertion. That failure is the missing build, never your delta — build and re-run before reading anything into it. `commands.test` is `pnpm build && pnpm test` for this reason.

The suite is slow — budget 3 to 5 minutes for `commands.test`, not seconds. Measured on this commit: `pnpm build && pnpm test` 3m23s end to end (exit 0, 70 files / 642 tests), of which apps/api is 122s (28 files, 283 tests) and apps/worker 56s; the other four packages together take under 16s. Across runs the same command has measured 2m17s, 2m30s, 3m13s, 3m23s and 4m15s depending on how busy the runner is, so treat 2-5 minutes as the range rather than any one number. Nearly every test boots a fresh PGlite Postgres and replays every migration, so it is not hung; budget for it rather than killing it, and do not speed it up by cutting the vitest timeouts.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is required: pnpm-lock.yaml is committed and CI uses the frozen flag, so a dependency added without updating the lockfile fails CI at the install step, before any test output exists to explain it.
Relative imports need the `.js` extension (NodeNext). Omitting it typechecks in some editors but fails `tsc -p tsconfig.json` and at runtime — this is the single most common build break here.

packages/db's build copies `migrations/` into `dist/migrations` as a second step; a migration added without running `pnpm build` is invisible to `runMigrations` in a built (Docker) image even though the tests, which read the source directory directly, pass.

The api and worker both run `runMigrations` on boot and would race, so the runner takes a Postgres advisory lock (packages/db/src/migrate.ts). Do not 'simplify' that lock away — without it Postgres fails one process with a duplicate-key error on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.

The webhook route deliberately sits outside session/CSRF middleware and reads the raw body in `preParsing` for HMAC verification. Moving it behind the normal request pipeline, or letting JSON parsing consume the body first, breaks signature verification for every delivery.

GitHub forbids Actions secret names starting with `GITHUB_`, so the deploy workflow takes `GH_APP_*` / `GH_OAUTH_*` and writes them to the VPS `.env` as `GITHUB_APP_*` / `GITHUB_OAUTH_*`. Also: those values must come from `env_file` only — adding `${GITHUB_APP_*}` to a compose `environment:` block blanks them via empty interpolation (noted in the deploy workflow and infra/docker-compose.deploy.yml).
`DEV_FAKE_LOGIN=1` bypasses GitHub OAuth entirely. It is a local-development switch and must never reach a deployed environment.

The product is called **Compass**; the code is still called `console`, on purpose. 709f5da (#82) renamed only user-facing strings — page title, header, the notes the Console posts on GitHub, the default GitHub App name, the insight prompt, docs and scripts. Everything an identifier touches was deliberately left alone: the repo is `software-factory-view`, the package scopes are `@console/api|web|worker|core|db|insight`, the env vars are `CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY` / `CONSOLE_HOST` / `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, the compose project and images are `factory-console` / `factory-console-app` / `factory-console-web`, the api container is `factory-console-api-1`, the deploy directory is `~/factory-console` and the health endpoint still answers `{"ok":true,"service":"console-api"}`. Do not 'finish' the rename: renaming a package scope, an env var or a container name breaks the deployed stack and the health checks, and it is not a tidy-up anyone asked for. New user-facing copy says Compass; new identifiers follow the existing `console` naming.

Base implementation PRs on `main`. `.github/factory-branches.json` sets `"required": false` with no `epics` key, which is this repo opting out of the staging step on purpose (its comment: the Console is released from `main`, and its deploy workflow runs on every merge there). So there is no release train to assemble and no epic branch: a task PR bases on `main`, and merging it deploys to production. Do not infer a staging step from the policy file merely mentioning `"staging": "staging"` — `required: false` is what decides.

A `staging` branch does physically exist, and it is dead: it sits at 011946f, 24 commits behind `main` and 0 ahead (verified with `git rev-list --left-right --count`), left behind by a Profiler run on 2026-10-13 that cut it before the policy was set to `required: false`. Nothing deploys from it and nothing merges into it. Do not base work on it, and do not read its existence as evidence of an integration branch.

FACTORY.md §8a layer 3 does not exist in this repo: .github/workflows/factory-branch-guard.yml was deleted in b91b168, so nothing detects a commit landing on `main` without a PR, or a merge that skipped staging. Two files still claim otherwise — the `_comment` in .github/factory-branches.json ("The branch guard still flags a commit that lands on `main` without a PR") and the "branch-guard workflow" mentioned in .github/REPOSITORY_SETTINGS.md. Protection here rests on the PreToolUse hook and the .claude/settings.json deny list only, plus whatever branch ruleset is configured server-side.

The workflow token cannot open pull requests in this repo: `POST /repos/.../pulls` returns 403 `GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests` (observed on six Profiler runs now — one on 2026-10-13 and five on 2026-10-31, the last re-verified at 79ffcf0). The token is the Actions workflow token, not a PAT: `gh api user` also 403s with `Resource not accessible by integration`. Two fixes, either one sufficient: turn on Settings -> Actions -> General -> *Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests* (.github/REPOSITORY_SETTINGS.md:53 says to leave it on exactly when the factory opens PRs with the workflow token here, which it does), or set the FACTORY_CROSS_REPO_TOKEN secret, which is not set in this repo today. Until then any role that must open a PR should push its branch and say on the issue that a human must open it, rather than failing silently.

An Action version bump still reaches the deploy path with nothing exercising it first — and since 79ffcf0 (#86) it gets even less. Both of deploy.yml's triggers carry `paths-ignore` including `.github/**`, and a dependabot `github_actions` PR touches nothing but `.github/workflows/**`: so the `check` job does not run on the pull request, and the merge to `main` matches the same filter, so neither the post-merge check nor the deploy runs either. CodeQL's `actions` language is a security scan, not a functional one. The bumped action is therefore first exercised by the next unrelated code deploy. For the `check` job's own actions (actions/checkout, pnpm/action-setup, actions/setup-node) a break at least halts the run before anything is deployed; appleboy/scp-action (image tarballs and the compose file) and appleboy/ssh-action (the remote deploy script) are worse — they first run during a real production deploy, after `check` has gone green. bde68c2 (#57) bumped scp-action 0.1.7->1.0.0 — a major — and ssh-action 1.0.3->1.2.5 that way. Read those steps' inputs against the action's release notes when such a bump appears, and run the first deploy after one from `workflow_dispatch` while you are watching, not from a merge.

`apps/web/vite.config.ts.timestamp-1786244617305-2049876fd0fad.mjs` is committed (confirmed with `git ls-files`) and .gitignore has no `vite.config.ts.timestamp-*` entry. Vite regenerates one of these on every config load, so `git add -A` sweeps a fresh copy into your commit. Add files by name, or add the ignore pattern as a deliberate fix.

The factory pipeline ignores issues from authors without write access: the job-level `if:` in .github/workflows/factory-pipeline.yml requires OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, a Bot sender, or a label applied by someone other than the author. An outside contributor's issue therefore sits with no `factory:*` label at all until a maintainer labels it. That is intended (it keeps untrusted text out of an agent that can push), but it looks exactly like a stalled pipeline.

A document PR can still deploy production, because deploy.yml's filter does not cover every path the factory writes. 79ffcf0 (#86) added `paths-ignore: ['.github/**', '**/*.md', 'docs/**']` to both triggers, so merging a markdown-only or workflow-only PR to `main` no longer deploys. But `openspec/**` is not in that list and only its `*.md` files are caught by the glob: every folder under openspec/changes/ carries a `.openspec.yaml` (verified — all six do), and `openspec/config.yaml` exists too, so a spec or design PR that adds or touches one of those YAML files DOES run a full production deploy. `.claude/**` is likewise uncovered. FACTORY.md §6 assumes document PRs deploy nothing; here that holds for pure-markdown gate PRs only. Check the file list before merging a document PR when production must stay still.
reuse_hotspots: packages/core/src — before adding a helper, check here: factory.ts (label/state constants), markers.ts (hidden-comment parse/emit), derive.ts and phases.ts (factory state derivation), crypto.ts (envelope encrypt/decrypt), config.ts (env schema), github.ts (the whole REST surface, App JWT and OAuth — including `getFileAtRef` on the shared `RepoReader` and `UserClient.putFile` for committing a file as the user), credentials.ts (App credential resolution, database-first with env fallback). It is re-exported wholesale from packages/core/src/index.ts.

packages/core/src, the factory-policy half — epic-status.ts, next-step.ts, start-gate.ts, plan-tests.ts, test-verdict.ts, bug-report.ts, testing-policy.ts, orchestrator.ts and orchestrator-client.ts. Any question of the form 'may the Console offer this control?' or 'what does this state mean?' is probably already answered by one of these. Check before writing the condition into a route or a component. In particular `effectiveStage()` in epic-status.ts (added in f499aa5, #81) is how an epic's real progress is derived: an epic holds `factory:design-approved` for its whole build, so its own label is NOT where it is — the stage of its slowest task is. Never recompute that from labels in a route or a page.

apps/api/src/context.ts — `requireAuth`, `resolveSession`, `userClient` and the `AppDeps`/`RequestCtx` types. Any new route needs these rather than its own auth path. apps/api/src/gh-write.ts and user-token.ts hold the authoritative-write and token-renewal paths; apps/api/src/start-gate.ts, expedite.ts, attention.ts and threads.ts are the per-feature helpers routes already share. For approvers specifically, start-gate.ts has both shapes already: `loadApproversForGate` (estate-wide, for the queue) and `repoApprovers` (one repo, one gate, with `staging` falling back to `release` as the router does) — use the second for any permission decision about a single PR or repo. `loadOrg(…, { admin: true })` from routes/settings.ts is the org-admin gate every configuration write shares.
apps/api/src/routes/read.ts — `loadEpic` and the epic/repo/org lookup helpers other route modules already import. apps/api/src/render.ts is the single markdown sanitiser.

packages/db/src/schema.ts — 30 `pgTable` declarations; check for an existing table or column before adding one. Several concerns that look separate already have homes here: threads and threadEntries, decisions, gateViews, auditLog, notifications, artifactCache, onboardingRuns, reconcileRuns, and `webhookDeliveries` — the at-least-once delivery ledger that makes webhook handling idempotent. There is no bug-report table: bugs are GitHub issues, projected like any other.

apps/worker/src/artifacts.ts and project.ts — projection and repair helpers (`refreshRepoProfile`, `repairDependencies`, `projectIssue`, `projectPull`, …) reused by both the ingest worker and the reconciler. reconcile.ts holds the sweep itself and openspec.ts the change-folder scaffolding.

apps/web/src/api.ts (the fetch wrapper with the CSRF header), apps/web/src/lib/ (board.ts, filter.tsx, labels.ts, reauth.ts, and work.ts — added in #84/#85), apps/web/src/theme.ts, and apps/web/src/components/ — the SPA's shared pieces; pages should compose these rather than re-implement fetching, filtering, label rendering or re-auth handling. In particular lib/work.ts owns the redesign's five-step rail: `stageOf` folds the factory's many label states into clarify/design/build/test/release, and `buildWork`, `decisionCards` and `STAGE_LABEL` derive the Work list and Decisions queue from three reads the API already serves. A page that needs a stage name calls `stageOf`; it does not re-map labels of its own.

health_checks: curl -fsS "${PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-https://sf.genaipeople.com}/api/health"   # expects {"ok":true,"service":"console-api"} — the route is registered in apps/api/src/app.ts. The authoritative origin is the PUBLIC_ORIGIN variable on the `production` GitHub Environment; the fallback here is the value documented in deploy.yml and the README, not one this run could confirm against a live host.
ssh $DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST 'cd ~/factory-console && docker compose ps'   # every service up; postgres and redis report healthy

PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://sf.genaipeople.com ./scripts/verify-public-origin.sh   # repo-local smoke test: asserts the origin serves the Console (nginx SPA at /, {"ok":true,"service":"console-api"} at /api/health) and NOT the LangGraph orchestrator, which shares the VPS and has taken this hostname before. deploy.yml runs it as its last step.
notes: Deploy is .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Since 79ffcf0 (#86) its `check` job (typecheck + build + test) runs on pull requests too, and the `deploy` job is skipped there (`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`): only a push to `main` — or Run workflow — deploys, which builds both images, scps tarballs to the VPS, docker loads them, runs docker compose up in ~/factory-console, then scripts/verify-public-origin.sh. A merge to main IS the production deploy — there is no staging step to catch a bad change first. Both triggers skip changes matching `paths-ignore` (`.github/**`, `**/*.md`, `docs/**`), so a markdown-only or workflow-only merge deploys nothing; see gotchas for what that filter misses.

A PR now carries a real suite verdict, so a green `typecheck-test-build` check is evidence the suite passed — unless the PR touches only `.github/**`, `**/*.md` or `docs/**`, which triggers no check at all. Nothing runs the suite anywhere but deploy.yml. Deploys queue one behind another and never cancel, while a PR's check is per-branch and is cancelled by a newer push. These health checks describe production only: never report a staging health check, because there is nothing to run one against.

The workflow's own gate polls the api container for `healthy` for 3 minutes and fails the deploy if it never gets there, dumping `docker compose ps` and the last 100 api log lines. That failure halts the release: the previous containers are already gone by then, so the site is down until it is fixed or rolled back.

Migrations run automatically at api and worker boot. A migration that fails leaves the api container unhealthy and the deploy red — check the api logs first when a deploy fails immediately after a schema change.

The deploy pre-flight refuses to run unless every one of DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER, DEPLOY_KEY, CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY, DB_PASSWORD, PUBLIC_ORIGIN, GH_APP_ID, GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, GH_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GH_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GH_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET is set on the `production` GitHub Environment.

CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY must never be rotated casually: it decrypts every stored OAuth token, the GitHub App private key and the artifact cache. Losing or changing it means every user must sign in again and the App must be re-registered.

Traefik routes Host(CONSOLE_HOST) on the shared `lighthouse-network` docker network to this stack's nginx. If that network or the Traefik instance is missing, the containers come up healthy and the site is still unreachable — check from outside, not only from the host.
